case_selection: Five purposively selected state cases illustrating distinct institutions and remedies; not a census of all states, laws, or moratoriums.

states.authority: Governor, state legislature, regulators and local permitting bodies have different powers
states.observed_remedy: Public support for at least a one-year ban; no enacted statewide moratorium established by this evidence packet
states.election_link: November 3 gubernatorial and legislative contests; governor's new term begins January 2027. August 11 nomination resolution and turnout-screen differences confound attribution of the odds change.
states.cross_party_status: Opposition to the cost-benefit balance spans Republican, independent and Democratic respondents; party-specific support for the same ban is not established here.
states.cash_flow_channel: Prospective permitting, infrastructure cost allocation and development timing; do not assume all existing facilities are affected equally.
states.interpretation: Broad concern is established; data centers are a much smaller stated current priority than inflation.

states.authority: Public Utilities Commission of Ohio; AEP Ohio tariff process
states.observed_remedy: Separate data-center tariff addressing stranded infrastructure and cost shifting; order also called for lifting AEP Ohio's connection moratorium
states.election_link: Existing regulatory action predates this campaign; changing the governor does not itself rewrite every approved utility tariff.
states.cross_party_status: This regulatory order does not measure partisan voter agreement.
states.cash_flow_channel: Customer commitments and minimum charges can protect utility recovery while raising the hurdle for new data-center customers.
states.interpretation: Cost protection can enable connection growth; it is not equivalent to banning development.

states.authority: Governor and permitting agencies; utility tariffs still require the appropriate PUC process
states.observed_remedy: GRID participation and local-approval sequencing for new applications above 25 MW; data centers removed from Fast Track; advocacy for protective tariffs
states.election_link: Executive implementation is already underway before the November gubernatorial vote; distinguish incumbent actions from future legislative capacity.
states.cross_party_status: An executive order is institutional action, not a measure of bipartisan voter or legislative support.
states.cash_flow_channel: Timing, project financing and infrastructure obligations may change without a universal ban or cancellation of all orders.
states.interpretation: The immediate investable risk is conditional development and who pays, not a categorical statewide prohibition.

states.authority: Governor, legislature, Department of Energy Resources and utility regulator
states.observed_remedy: Moratorium bill veto sustained; advisory council created; recommendations due January 29, 2027
states.election_link: The recommendations fall after the election; the sustained veto shows that public pressure and enacted restrictions can diverge.
states.cross_party_status: Governor supported a temporary moratorium with a project exemption; not a simple pro-development versus anti-development division.
states.cash_flow_channel: Project-specific employment and local tax-base benefits can alter exemptions and legislative compromises.
states.interpretation: Policy design and exemptions matter; the advisory council cannot be counted as a binding moratorium.

states.observed_remedy: Enacted automated-decision rules covering consequential decisions; major developer duties and attorney-general rules from January 2027
states.election_link: Implementation follows the election but arises from an existing law; a new governor does not make the law disappear automatically.
states.cross_party_status: Recorded majorities are 34-1 Senate and 57-6 House; no party affiliation is inferred from vote totals.
states.cash_flow_channel: Documentation, notices, human review and record retention affect covered applications; do not apply indiscriminately to every AI revenue stream.
states.interpretation: Concrete state compliance risk exists even without a new federal AI act.

institutional_scenarios.legislative_route: Aligned agenda can facilitate tax, spending and appointments, subject to chamber rules and internal agreement.
institutional_scenarios.constraint: Ordinary legislation still faces Senate procedure; reconciliation is constrained and not a universal route.
institutional_scenarios.equity_question: Which current tax, energy, immigration or trade policies persist, and which new proposals actually alter baseline cash flows?

institutional_scenarios.legislative_route: Cross-chamber bargains are needed; Senate confirmation and oversight capacity changes.
institutional_scenarios.constraint: A rare combination in the quoted market is still a distinct organizational outcome, not the product of independent marginals.
institutional_scenarios.equity_question: Stress policy delay, appointments and funding compromises; avoid assuming either party's full programme.

institutional_scenarios.legislative_route: House oversight and bargaining over budgets increase; Senate and presidency constrain new legislation.
institutional_scenarios.constraint: A House victory is not a presidential transition or immediate repeal of executive policies.
institutional_scenarios.equity_question: Separate reduced probability of new legislation from continued executive enforcement, state policy and funding negotiation risk.

institutional_scenarios.legislative_route: Both chambers can set a different legislative agenda and strengthen oversight; Senate confirmations change.
institutional_scenarios.constraint: Presentment and veto still matter; ordinary simple majorities do not guarantee enactment or a veto override.
institutional_scenarios.equity_question: Model feasible bargains and oversight pressure rather than a wholesale implementation of campaign promises.

fed_background.date_status: Standing institutional background, retrieved September 9, 2026; not a new campaign event
fed_background.claim: Monetary-policy decisions do not require approval by the president or Congress. Electoral outcomes can affect fiscal policy and appointments, but do not mechanically set the policy-rate path.

common_constraints: The joint contracts refer to organizational control in February 2027, not identical settlement rules to election-winner contracts.
Report quoted bid/ask and midpoint as observed; do not normalize the sum or multiply marginal probabilities.
The presidency is held fixed as a scenario convention, subject to constitutional succession.
A state governor's victory does not imply control of both chambers, local zoning or every regulator.
Markets resolving before January 2027 do not directly measure laws enacted by the incoming Congress.
Policy stage classifications are nominal categories, not ordinal enactment probabilities.
